intro: A layer receives the gradient of a later computation. The chain rule tells us how that signal changes its inputs, weights, and bias.
task: For Y = X @ W + b, return a dictionary containing dx, dw, and db given the incoming gradient grad_output.
requirements: X has shape (n,d), W has shape (d,o), and grad_output has shape (n,o). All dimensions must be positive.
Return NumPy arrays: dx (n,d), dw (d,o), and db (o,).
Sum bias and weight contributions over the batch. Do not introduce an additional average.
Accept numeric lists or arrays. Reject incompatible, non-finite, or non-2D inputs with ValueError; leave inputs unchanged.

hints.title: Write down shapes
hints.body: For dx, combine (n,o) with a transposed (d,o) weight matrix.

hints.title: Accumulate weight contributions
hints.body: Each input feature contributes to each output. X.T @ grad_output sums these outer products.

hints.title: Do not average twice
hints.body: The incoming gradient already reflects any averaging performed by the loss.

explanation: The vector-Jacobian product avoids constructing a large Jacobian explicitly. Matrix multiplication performs the same chain-rule accumulation.
dx = G @ W.T, dw = X.T @ G, and db = sum(G, axis=0). Each expression can be checked by its shape.
The batch reduction belongs to the loss definition. Adding a second division by n here would silently shrink every upstream gradient.
formula: dX = G Wᵀ · dW = Xᵀ G · db = Σᵢ Gᵢ
